sammendrag: Two-year postsecondary institutions, commonly referred to as community colleges, are an important source of higher education and career training for adult literacy learners in the United States. Most adult literacy learners are referred to developmental reading and writing courses upon college entry; in some cases, low-literacy learners are served through the college's adult basic education program. In this chapter we discuss the current landscape of developmental reading and writing education in the United States, including how developmental coursework has traditionally been structured and delivered, and the role of adult basic education providers at community colleges. The authors identify ways in which developmental education poses barriers to student progression and college completion and review promising approaches to educating adult literacy learners within community colleges. Two approaches with positive outcomes for adult literacy learners in community colleges are highlighted: an accelerated developmental English course and a pre-matriculation intervention located in a continuing education division.
tittel: Research on Developmental Education Instruction for Adult Literacy Learners
